title: Earth united under one government
summary: The last holdout nation-states join Earth's world government, finishing the unification that began with the European Hegemony; humanity now faces the stars as a single polity.

title: First contact with the Klingon Empire
summary: The Klingon courier Klaang crash-lands in a cornfield near Broken Bow, Oklahoma, pursued by Suliban; Earth's decision to fly him home to Qo'noS becomes humanity's first real dealing with the Klingon Empire.
conflict: TNG 'First Contact' recalls a 'disastrous contact' with the Klingons that led to decades of war; ENT's 2151 contact is tense but no war follows for generations.

title: Enterprise NX-01 launched
summary: Earth's first warp-five starship leaves spacedock under Captain Jonathan Archer, weeks ahead of schedule, to return Klaang home. Its launch anniversary is later celebrated as Frontier Day.

title: Temporal Cold War first detected
summary: Archer's crew learns the Suliban Cabal takes orders from a faceless patron in the future. By autumn, crewman Daniels reveals himself as a 31st-century agent fighting a cold war waged across time.

title: First contact with the Andorians
summary: At the Vulcan monastery of P'Jem, Archer's crew meets Andorian commandos led by Shran and discovers that the Vulcans hide a listening post there, exposing a long feud between the two peoples.

title: Ferengi raiders board Enterprise
summary: Ferengi looters sedate Enterprise's crew and ransack the ship before Archer and Trip Tucker outwit them. Neither side learns the other's species name.
conflict: Starfleet's official first contact with the Ferengi is dated 2364 (TNG 'The Last Outpost'), two centuries after this unnamed encounter.

title: Archer pulled into a ruined future
summary: After the Cabal frames Enterprise for destroying the Paraagan II colony, Daniels pulls Archer into the 31st century, only to find it erased by the disruption to history. Returning Archer to 2152 restores the future.

title: First contact with the Romulans
summary: Enterprise strays into a cloaked minefield around a Romulan world and is ordered out by warships it can barely see. It is Earth's first contact with the Star Empire, made without a face-to-face meeting.

title: Archer brokers Andorian–Vulcan ceasefire
summary: Acting as a mediator trusted by both sides, Archer helps Ambassador Soval and Commander Shran agree to a ceasefire over the disputed planet Weytahn, the first sign of Earth as a bridge between rival powers.

title: First contact with the Tholians
summary: Enterprise recovers a derelict time pod from the future and finds both the Suliban and the previously unknown Tholians determined to seize it. This is Earth's first encounter with the crystalline species.

title: Borg drones revived in the Arctic
summary: Researchers dig up drones from the Borg sphere destroyed in 2063; the drones assimilate them and escape. Enterprise destroys them, but not before they send a signal toward the Delta Quadrant that will take two centuries to arrive.
conflict: The Federation's official first contact with the Borg is dated 2365 (TNG 'Q Who'); the 2153 attackers were never identified by name.

title: Xindi probe attacks Earth
summary: A probe fired from the Delphic Expanse cuts a burning path from Florida to Venezuela, killing seven million people. It is a test run for a weapon meant to destroy Earth.

title: Enterprise enters the Delphic Expanse
summary: Recalled and refitted, Enterprise and a detachment of MACOs cross into the anomaly-ridden Delphic Expanse and make first contact with the Xindi, a people of five species united by a council.

title: Xindi superweapon destroyed at Earth
summary: Archer and his Xindi allies destroy the weapon as it reaches Earth, foiling the Sphere-Builders' plan to stop the Federation from ever forming. Enterprise then vanishes into an altered 1944.

title: Temporal Cold War declared over
summary: Enterprise helps destroy the Na'kuhl leader Vosk's temporal conduit in an alternate 1944, undoing his Nazi-aided incursion. Daniels declares that the Temporal Cold War is over.

title: Augments nearly start a Klingon war
summary: Genetically engineered Augments raised by Dr. Arik Soong from 20th-century embryos seize a Klingon ship and plot to provoke war with the Empire. Enterprise stops them, and Soong turns to cybernetics.

title: Syrrannites reform the Vulcan government
summary: The Kir'Shara, holding Surak's original writings, is recovered, and Administrator V'Las is exposed as a Romulan collaborator. The Vulcan High Command is dissolved and Vulcan's stance toward Earth softens.

title: Babel Crisis unites the founding powers
summary: A telepathically piloted Romulan drone ship attacks Andorians and Tellarites to wreck a peace conference on Babel. Earth, Vulcan, Andoria and Tellar pool their ships and stop it, cooperating as allies for the first time.

title: Section 31 recruits within Starfleet
summary: Lieutenant Malcolm Reed's handler, Harris, reveals a covert branch working inside Starfleet. Two centuries later Section 31 claims its authority from the original Starfleet Charter.

title: Columbia NX-02 launched
summary: Earth's second warp-five ship leaves drydock under Captain Erika Hernandez, doubling Starfleet's deep-space fleet.

title: Klingon augment virus spreads
summary: A Klingon attempt to breed warriors from Augment DNA unleashes a deadly plague. Phlox's cure saves the Empire, but millions of Klingons and their descendants lose their cranial ridges for generations.

title: Coalition of Planets conference
summary: Humans, Vulcans, Andorians, Tellarites, Rigelians, Denobulans and Coridanites meet on Earth to form a Coalition of Planets. The talks survive the xenophobic Terra Prime movement's seizure of a Martian weapons array.

title: Terrans seize the time-lost USS Defiant
summary: In the mirror universe, the ISS Enterprise finds the USS Defiant — lost from the prime universe in 2268 — in Tholian space. The mirror Archer seizes it, and Hoshi Sato takes it to claim the title of Empress.
sources: In A Mirror, Darkly, Part II (episode)

title: Earth–Romulan War begins
summary: Years of Romulan sabotage erupt into open war with United Earth and its allies. The war is fought ship to ship with primitive atomic weapons, and neither side ever sees the other's face.
sources: In A Mirror, Darkly, Part II (episode)

title: Battle of Cheron ends the Romulan War
summary: An alliance of Earth, Vulcan, Andoria and Tellar deals the Romulans a crushing defeat at Cheron, effectively ending the four-year war.
sources: In A Mirror, Darkly, Part II (episode)

title: Romulan Neutral Zone established
summary: Peace is negotiated entirely over subspace radio, and the treaty creates a Neutral Zone that either side may enter only as an act of war. The Zone stands until Romulus is destroyed in 2387.

title: Enterprise NX-01 retired
summary: After ten years of service, Earth's pioneering starship is decommissioned on the eve of the Federation's founding, with Archer on his way to the charter ceremony.

title: United Federation of Planets founded
summary: Earth, Vulcan, Andoria and Tellar sign the Federation Charter in San Francisco, turning their wartime alliance into a permanent union. Starfleet becomes the new Federation's service.

title: Starfleet Academy chartered for the Federation
summary: Earth's existing Space Academy is incorporated into the new Federation Starfleet under the motto Ex Astris, Scientia. It will train Starfleet officers for the next nine centuries.

title: USS Franklin vanishes
summary: The first Earth ship capable of warp 4 disappears in the Gagarin Radiation Belt. It has been pulled to a distant nebula, where its stranded captain Balthazar Edison becomes the warlord Krall.

title: USS Essex lost at Mab-Bu VI
summary: The Daedalus-class Essex is destroyed by an electromagnetic storm near a moon of Mab-Bu VI. Its wreck stays undiscovered until the Enterprise-D finds it in 2368.

title: USS Archon lost at Beta III
summary: The starship Archon is destroyed at Beta III and its crew absorbed into a society controlled by the computer Landru, a fate uncovered only when Kirk's Enterprise visits a century later.

title: Money falls out of use on Earth
summary: Earth's New World Economy takes shape, and money 'goes the way of the dinosaur'; material want gives way to the pursuit of self-improvement.

title: Archer becomes Federation President
summary: Jonathan Archer, former captain of the NX-01 and ambassador to Andoria, begins an eight-year term as President of the United Federation of Planets.
sources: In A Mirror, Darkly, Part II (episode)

title: Mining colony founded on Janus VI
summary: Settlers open a pergium mine on Janus VI that becomes a key supplier for a dozen worlds, unaware they are sharing the planet with the silicon-based Horta.

title: Federation–Klingon cold war begins
summary: Relations with the Klingon Empire sour into roughly seventy years of hostility — border disputes, brush wars and arms races that end only with the Khitomer Accords of 2293.
sources: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
In A Mirror, Darkly, Part II (episode)

title: Narada incursion splits off Kelvin reality
summary: Nero's mining ship Narada, thrown back from 2387 through a red-matter singularity, destroys the USS Kelvin near the Klingon border. The incursion branches off an alternate reality in which history unfolds differently from here on.

title: Red Angel time suit first used
summary: Section 31's Project Daedalus, begun after learning of Klingon time-travel research, yields a working time suit. When Klingons attack Doctari Alpha, Dr. Gabrielle Burnham uses it and is flung 950 years ahead, becoming anchored to 3186.

title: Daystrom invents duotronic computing
summary: At 24, Dr. Richard Daystrom makes the duotronic breakthrough that becomes the basis of Starfleet computers for some eighty years and wins him the Nobel and Zee-Magnees prizes.

title: USS Enterprise (NCC-1701) launched
summary: The Constitution-class Enterprise enters service under Captain Robert April, later passing to Christopher Pike and then James T. Kirk. It serves as the Federation flagship until 2285.

title: Battle of Donatu V
summary: Federation and Klingon forces fight an inconclusive battle over the disputed region around Donatu V and Sherman's Planet, one of the few open clashes of the cold war.
conflict: In 2256 Captain Georgiou says 'almost no one has seen a Klingon in a hundred years' (DIS 'The Vulcan Hello'), which is hard to square with a shooting war only eleven years earlier.

title: Tarsus IV massacre
summary: When a fungus destroys the colony's food stores, Governor Kodos orders the execution of 4,000 of Tarsus IV's 8,000 colonists. A teenage James Kirk is among the survivors who witness it.

title: Omega molecule disaster at Lantaru
summary: Physicist Ketteract synthesizes a single Omega molecule in a secret station in the Lantaru sector. It explodes, killing him and 126 other scientists and wrecking subspace for light-years; Starfleet covers it up and issues the Omega Directive.

title: Talos IV placed under quarantine
summary: After Captain Pike's Enterprise is held by the telepathic illusion-casting Talosians, Starfleet issues General Order 7, forbidding contact with Talos IV on pain of death.

title: USS Discovery enters service
summary: The Crossfield-class science vessel Discovery, fresh from the shipyards, is fitted with an experimental propulsion system and placed under Captain Gabriel Lorca for secret wartime research.

title: Battle of the Binary Stars
summary: T'Kuvma lights the Klingon beacon at the Binary Stars and rallies the 24 Great Houses. The battle that follows, the first face-to-face clash with Klingons in a century, costs thousands of Starfleet lives and opens the Federation–Klingon War.

title: Spore drive jumps into service
summary: Discovery's displacement-activated spore hub drive uses the mycelial network to jump across vast distances instantly, giving Starfleet a strategic edge in the war.

title: Earliest known Federation–Cardassian contact
summary: Service records show Captain Christopher Pike, and later Una Chin-Riley, holding the Legate's Crest of Valor, a Cardassian decoration — evidence that the Federation had dealings with the Cardassian Union by the 2250s.
conflict: No on-screen date for first contact with the Cardassians has ever been given; the two peoples had crossed paths as early as 2152.

title: Terran Emperor brought to the prime universe
summary: Escaping the collapse of her empire, the mirror universe's Emperor Philippa Georgiou is beamed aboard Discovery and brought into the prime universe, where she is later recruited by Section 31.
sources: The War Without, The War Within (episode)

title: Klingon War ends under Chancellor L'Rell
summary: With Qo'noS threatened by a hydrogen bomb, Burnham hands the detonator to L'Rell, who uses it to force the Great Houses to accept her as Chancellor and ends the war.

title: Seven red signals appear across the galaxy
summary: Seven unexplained bursts appear across the galaxy, drawing Discovery and Pike's Enterprise into the Red Angel mystery; the signals are later found to come from Burnham herself in a time suit.

title: Kelpiens freed from the Ba'ul
summary: Discovery learns the Ba'ul have culled the Kelpiens for millennia to stop their natural transformation. With the Red Angel's intervention, the Kelpiens are freed to mature and begin their rise to the stars.

title: Vulcan destroyed (Kelvin reality)
summary: In the alternate reality, Nero drills to Vulcan's core and ignites red matter, collapsing the planet into a black hole; about 10,000 Vulcans survive to found New Vulcan.

title: Discovery leaps 930 years into the future
summary: To keep the Sphere's archive away from the rogue AI Control, Burnham leads Discovery through a wormhole to the future. Starfleet classifies the ship and its spore drive and orders the survivors never to speak of them.

title: Khan's attack on Starfleet (Kelvin reality)
summary: In the alternate reality, a revived Khan bombs a London archive and Starfleet headquarters, and the dreadnought Vengeance crashes into San Francisco before he is returned to cryosleep.

title: General Order 1 becomes the Prime Directive
summary: After Pike's crew intervenes on Kiley 279, the Federation Council tightens enforcement of General Order 1 and renames it the Prime Directive.

title: Time agents battle over Khan's history
summary: A dying agent of a future Department of Temporal Investigations sends La'An Noonien-Singh to 2022 to stop Romulan agents from killing the young Khan — one front of temporal wars that shifted the Eugenics Wars later in history.

title: Una Chin-Riley granted asylum
summary: Charged with hiding her genetically modified Illyrian heritage to join Starfleet, Commander Una Chin-Riley is instead granted asylum, a first crack in the Federation's rigid ban on genetic modification.

title: Gorn raid Finibus III
summary: The Gorn wipe out the Finibus III colony and ambush Pike's Enterprise, which escapes by using the system's black hole as cover. Officially, the Gorn remain a species never encountered.

title: Gorn seize Parnassus Beta
summary: A Gorn strike force destroys the USS Stardiver and USS Cayuga, abducts the Parnassus Beta colonists and declares a demarcation line through the system. Starfleet orders the Enterprise to withdraw rather than risk war.
conflict: Memory Alpha itself dates this attack to 2259, 2260 and 2261 on different pages; the next episode's Federation centennial party points to 2261.

title: Gorn armada forced into hibernation
summary: Pike's crew rescues the Parnassus colonists and flies between binary stars to trigger an artificial coronal mass ejection. The storm drives a massing Gorn armada into a long hibernation cycle.

title: Federation celebrates its centennial
summary: The Federation marks one hundred years since its founding with a celebration attended by the Enterprise crew.

title: Starfleet trials its first holodeck
summary: La'An Noonien-Singh stress-tests a new holographic recreation room aboard the Enterprise, an early form of the holodecks later common on starships.

title: Enterprise thrown back to the Cretaceous
summary: A category 10 interstellar squall hurls Pike's Enterprise 66 million years into the past, to the end-Cretaceous extinction, where the crew finds a doomed civilization on Mars and becomes part of a predestination paradox.

title: Ambassador Spock dies (Kelvin reality)
summary: The elder Spock of the prime reality, stranded since 2258 in the Kelvin reality, dies on New Vulcan after helping rebuild the Vulcan people.

title: Kirk begins the five-year mission
summary: Captain James T. Kirk takes the Enterprise on its historic five-year mission of exploration, a voyage later generations treat as the model of what Starfleet is for.
sources: Where No Man Has Gone Before (episode)

title: Borg destroy the El-Aurian homeworld
summary: The Borg ravage the El-Aurian homeworld; the survivors scatter as refugees across the galaxy, some reaching Federation space aboard the Lakul in 2293.

title: First visual contact with the Romulans
summary: A cloaked Romulan warship destroys Federation outposts along the Neutral Zone. Kirk's crew intercepts its bridge signal and becomes the first to see Romulans, who turn out to be of Vulcan descent.

title: Khan Noonien Singh revived and exiled
summary: The Enterprise finds the sleeper ship SS Botany Bay adrift with Khan Noonien Singh and his Augments in stasis. Khan tries to seize the ship and is exiled with his followers to Ceti Alpha V.

title: Enterprise slingshots back to 1969
summary: Thrown back to Earth in 1969 by a black star, the Enterprise returns by whipping around the Sun, pioneering the slingshot effect as a means of time travel.

title: Official first contact with the Gorn
summary: The Gorn destroy the Federation outpost on Cestus III, which they consider their territory. The Metrons force Kirk and the Gorn captain into single combat, and Kirk's refusal to kill earns both ships a reprieve.
conflict: SNW shows Gorn attacks on Federation ships and colonies from the 2230s to 2261 that never made it into the official record, so Starfleet still counts 2267 as first contact.

title: Guardian of Forever discovered
summary: The Enterprise finds an ancient, sentient time portal on a desolate world. A delirious McCoy changes 1930s Earth history through it, and Kirk and Spock must follow him to set history right.
sources: The City on the Edge of Forever (episode)

title: Organians impose the Treaty of Organia
summary: As a Federation–Klingon war breaks out over Organia, the Organians, beings of pure energy, disable both fleets and impose a peace treaty on the two powers.

title: Kirk seeds reform in the mirror universe
summary: A transporter accident swaps Kirk's party with their Terran Empire counterparts. Kirk urges the mirror Spock to reform the Empire, reforms that later leave it open to conquest by a Klingon–Cardassian Alliance.
conflict: Records credit Kirk's crew as the first visitors to the mirror universe, but Discovery crossed over a decade earlier in 2257, a voyage Starfleet later classified.

title: USS Defiant lost in interphase
summary: The Constitution-class Defiant vanishes into interphase in Tholian space. It resurfaces a century in the past in the mirror universe, where the Terran Empire seizes it.

title: Starfleet steals a Romulan cloaking device
summary: On a covert mission, Kirk and Spock steal a Romulan cloaking device and learn that the Romulans now field Klingon-designed warships.

title: Kirk's five-year mission ends
summary: The Enterprise returns home after five years of exploration and goes into a long refit; Kirk is promoted to admiral.

title: V'Ger threatens Earth
summary: A vast machine entity destroys three Klingon cruisers and Epsilon IX on its way to Earth. The refitted Enterprise finds it is Voyager 6, grown sentient; it merges with Commander Decker to evolve.
conflict: No year is stated on screen; dialogue about Kirk's time away from the Enterprise puts the film around 2272–2273.

title: USS Bozeman caught in a time loop
summary: The Soyuz-class Bozeman vanishes in the Typhon Expanse, trapped in a temporal causality loop. It emerges unchanged in 2368, ninety years later.

title: Genesis Device detonated in the Mutara Nebula
summary: Khan escapes Ceti Alpha V, hijacks the Reliant and seizes the Genesis Device. Its detonation forms a new planet from the nebula, and Spock dies saving the Enterprise.
sources: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

title: USS Excelsior commissioned
summary: Starfleet's transwarp prototype enters service. The transwarp drive fails its trials, but the Excelsior design becomes a mainstay of the fleet, and the ship is later commanded by Hikaru Sulu.
sources: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock

title: Enterprise destroyed over Genesis
summary: Kirk scuttles the aging Enterprise to kill a Klingon boarding party over the unstable Genesis Planet, ending forty years of service. Spock's body, regenerated there, is later reunited with his katra.
sources: Star Trek III: The Search for Spock

title: Whale Probe cripples Earth
summary: An alien probe calling for the extinct humpback whales disables ships and devastates Earth's weather. Kirk's crew travels back to 1986 and brings two whales forward to answer it.
sources: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home

title: USS Enterprise-A commissioned
summary: Demoted to captain for his unauthorized rescue of Spock, Kirk is given a new Constitution-class ship bearing the name Enterprise, registry NCC-1701-A.
sources: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home

title: Nimbus III hostage crisis
summary: Sybok seizes the three consuls of the 'Planet of Galactic Peace' — a joint Federation, Klingon and Romulan colony — and uses the Enterprise to search for Sha Ka Ree.
sources: Star Trek V: The Final Frontier

title: Praxis explodes
summary: Over-mining and poor safety set off an explosion that destroys Praxis, the Klingon Empire's key energy-production moon. The ozone of Qo'noS is poisoned, giving the Empire about fifty years to live.
sources: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

title: Chancellor Gorkon assassinated
summary: Gorkon, who sought peace after Praxis, is killed aboard Kronos One by a Federation–Klingon–Romulan conspiracy against détente. Kirk and McCoy are framed and sent to Rura Penthe.
sources: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

title: Khitomer Accords signed
summary: At the Khitomer Conference, Chancellor Azetbur and the Federation President sign the accords that end some seventy years of hostility, the start of nearly a century of Federation–Klingon peace.
sources: Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

title: USS Enterprise-B launched
summary: Months after the Enterprise-A is decommissioned, the Excelsior-class Enterprise-B leaves spacedock under Captain John Harriman, not yet fully equipped, with Kirk, Scott and Chekov as guests.

title: Kirk lost in the Nexus
summary: On its maiden voyage the Enterprise-B rescues El-Aurian refugees from the Lakul and the Robert-Kirk. While Kirk modifies the deflector to free the ship from the energy ribbon, the section he is in is torn open, and he is presumed killed.

title: USS Jenolan crashes on a Dyson sphere
summary: The transport Jenolan crashes on the surface of a Dyson sphere. Montgomery Scott survives by suspending himself in the transporter buffer and is rescued 75 years later.

title: Tomed Incident; Romulans go silent
summary: A Federation–Romulan clash known as the Tomed Incident costs thousands of lives. Afterward the Romulan Star Empire withdraws from interstellar affairs for 53 years.

title: Treaty of Algeron signed
summary: The peace that follows the Tomed Incident reaffirms and redraws the Romulan Neutral Zone and commits the Federation to neither develop nor use cloaking technology.

title: Cardassian occupation of Bajor begins
summary: The Cardassian Union asserts control over Bajor, formally annexing it in 2328. Half a century of strip-mining, forced labor and atrocities follows, resisted by Bajoran cells.
conflict: Its length is given as forty years (TNG 'Ensign Ro'; Dukat in DS9 'Waltz'), fifty (the usual figure, giving 2319–2369) and sixty (DS9 'Emissary'); 'Things Past' would even imply 2316.

title: Section 31 secures the Godsend weapon
summary: A Section 31 team — including a young Lieutenant Rachel Garrett — recruits the exiled mirror-universe Emperor Philippa Georgiou to keep the Godsend, a Terran doomsday weapon, from being sold beyond the Federation's borders.

title: Enterprise-C lost at Narendra III
summary: Answering a distress call, Captain Rachel Garrett's Enterprise-C is destroyed defending the Klingon outpost on Narendra III from four Romulan warbirds. The sacrifice convinces the Klingons of Federation honor and cements their alliance.

title: Khitomer Massacre
summary: Using defense codes supplied by the Klingon traitor Ja'rod of the House of Duras, Romulan warships destroy the Khitomer colony. Among the few survivors is the young Worf, who is raised by Human foster parents.

title: Terok Nor built in orbit of Bajor
summary: Bajoran slave labor completes Terok Nor, a Cardassian ore-processing station over Bajor. After the occupation it becomes Deep Space 9.
sources: Wrongs Darker Than Death or Night (episode)
conflict: DS9 'Wrongs Darker Than Death or Night' shows the station nearly finished in 2346, while Odo's remark in 'Babel' implies it was built in 2351.

title: Federation–Cardassian War; Setlik III massacre
summary: Border conflict with the Cardassian Union turns to war. Believing Setlik III is a staging base, Cardassian troops massacre most of the outpost's inhabitants; skirmishes continue into the 2360s.

title: Stargazer lost at the Battle of Maxia
summary: An unidentified ship — later revealed as Ferengi — attacks Captain Picard's Stargazer at Maxia Zeta. Picard destroys it with the 'Picard maneuver' but must abandon his crippled ship.

title: USS Raven assimilated by the Borg
summary: Exobiologists Magnus and Erin Hansen, who had pursued rumors of the Borg without a flight plan, are assimilated with their daughter Annika. Nine years before official first contact, Annika becomes Seven of Nine.
conflict: Official first contact with the Borg is recorded in 2365; the Hansens' private research into them began a decade earlier.

title: Federation–Tzenkethi War
summary: The Federation fights a war against the Tzenkethi Coalition; Benjamin Sisko serves as first officer of the USS Okinawa under Captain Leyton during the conflict.

title: USS Enterprise-D launched
summary: The Galaxy-class Enterprise-D, built at Utopia Planitia, is launched from Mars and becomes the Federation flagship under Captain Jean-Luc Picard, carrying families as well as crew.

title: Q puts humanity on trial
summary: At Farpoint Station the omnipotent entity Q halts the Enterprise-D and charges humanity with savagery; the crew's handling of the Farpoint mystery wins a reprieve, and the Continuum's long interest in humans begins.

title: Official first contact with the Ferengi
summary: Near Delphi Ardu, the Enterprise-D meets the Ferengi face to face, putting a face to a species known until then only by rumor.
conflict: ENT 'Acquisition' shows Ferengi boarding the Enterprise NX-01 in 2151, but no names were exchanged, so the Federation dates first contact to 2364.

title: Parasites infiltrate Starfleet Command
summary: Neural parasites take over senior officers at Starfleet Command. Picard and Riker expose the plot and kill the mother creature, but a homing beacon has already been sent into deep space.

title: Romulans end their isolation
summary: Outposts on both sides of the Neutral Zone are wiped out — later blamed on the Borg — and a Romulan warbird confronts the Enterprise-D, ending the Empire's half-century of silence.

title: Data ruled free to choose
summary: A JAG hearing at Starbase 173 rules that the android Data is not Starfleet property and may refuse to be disassembled for study, a landmark for the rights of artificial life.

title: Official first contact with the Borg
summary: To humble Picard, Q flings the Enterprise-D 7,000 light-years to System J-25, where a Borg cube kills 18 crew before Picard asks Q for help. The Borg now know the Federation exists.
conflict: Earlier encounters were never named: drones from the 2063 sphere in 2153 (ENT 'Regeneration') and the Hansens' research from the 2350s.

title: Treaty ends the Cardassian War
summary: A peace treaty halts the Federation–Cardassian War after two decades of fighting, though mutual suspicion and border disputes remain.
conflict: TNG 'The Wounded' (2367) says the treaty was signed about a year earlier, but VOY 'Dreadnought' calls it 'the treaty of 2367'.

title: Enterprise-C emerges from a temporal rift
summary: Fleeing Narendra III through a rift, the Enterprise-C briefly creates a timeline in which the Federation is losing a war with the Klingons. Its crew returns to 2344 to die with honor and restore history.

title: Borg invade; Picard becomes Locutus
summary: A Borg cube wipes out the New Providence colony on Jouret IV, captures Picard and assimilates him as Locutus of Borg, the Collective's voice to humanity.

title: Battle of Wolf 359
summary: Forty Starfleet ships meet the cube at Wolf 359; 39 are destroyed and 11,000 people die. The Enterprise-D crew stops the cube in Earth orbit by reaching Picard through the Collective.
sources: The Best of Both Worlds, Part II (episode)

title: Gowron becomes Klingon Chancellor
summary: Chancellor K'mpec dies of slow poisoning. With Picard as Arbiter of Succession, Gowron is left as sole candidate after Worf kills Duras.

title: Klingon Civil War
summary: The House of Duras, secretly supplied by the Romulans, challenges Gowron. A Federation tachyon-detection blockade exposes the Romulan supply line and Gowron's side wins.

title: Spock goes underground on Romulus
summary: Ambassador Spock secretly joins a Romulan dissident movement seeking reunification with Vulcan. With Picard and Data he foils a Romulan plan to invade Vulcan under cover of the movement.

title: Cardassians withdraw from Bajor
summary: Worn down by the Bajoran Resistance, the Cardassian Union ends the occupation. Bajor's provisional government asks Starfleet to run the stripped station Terok Nor, now renamed Deep Space 9, under Commander Benjamin Sisko.

title: Bajoran wormhole discovered
summary: Sisko and Jadzia Dax find the first known stable wormhole, linking Bajor to the Gamma Quadrant. Its non-linear inhabitants — the Bajorans' Prophets — name Sisko their Emissary.

title: Progenitor message decoded
summary: Completing Professor Galen's research, Federation, Cardassian, Klingon and Romulan crews assemble a hidden message: an ancient humanoid species seeded life on many worlds, explaining why the quadrant's peoples look alike.

title: Clone of Kahless made Emperor
summary: Clerics of Boreth unveil a clone of the legendary Kahless. Gowron accepts him as a ceremonial Emperor, reviving a title vacant for three centuries.

title: Federation imposes a warp speed limit
summary: Hekaran scientists prove that high warp speeds tear subspace. The Federation limits ships to warp 5 except in emergencies, spurring nacelle designs that avoid the damage.
conflict: No repeal is ever mentioned, yet later ships routinely exceed warp 5 with no reference to the limit.

title: Illegal phasing cloak exposed
summary: Picard reveals to the Romulans that the lost USS Pegasus had tested a phasing cloak in violation of the Treaty of Algeron, a Starfleet cover-up dating back to 2358.

title: Treaty creates the Cardassian DMZ
summary: A new Federation–Cardassian treaty redraws the border and creates a Demilitarized Zone, leaving Federation colonists on worlds ceded to Cardassia.

title: Maquis resistance takes up arms
summary: Colonists who refuse to leave their homes in the DMZ, joined by sympathetic Starfleet officers, form the Maquis and wage guerrilla war on the Cardassians.

title: First contact with the Dominion
summary: Jem'Hadar soldiers declare the Gamma Quadrant closed to outsiders and destroy the Galaxy-class USS Odyssey, revealing the power of the Dominion beyond the wormhole.

title: Q's anti-time trial of humanity
summary: Q ends his trial by sending Picard across three time periods, where an anti-time anomaly spreading backward from the Devron system threatens to prevent life on Earth. Picard's insight collapses it.

title: USS Defiant assigned to Deep Space 9
summary: Starfleet sends the prototype Defiant — a warship designed to fight the Borg — to DS9, equipped with a Romulan cloak on loan in exchange for intelligence on the Dominion.

title: Founders revealed as Changelings
summary: Searching for the Dominion's rulers, the crew of the new USS Defiant finds that the Founders are shapeshifting Changelings — Odo's own people.

title: Temporal Prime Directive in force
summary: In 2368 Picard could only guess that the future might have such a rule; by 2371 Starfleet officers are bound by a Temporal Prime Directive forbidding interference with the course of history.

title: Voyager pulled into the Delta Quadrant
summary: Chasing a Maquis ship, the new Intrepid-class Voyager is pulled 70,000 light-years by the Caretaker. Janeway destroys the array to protect the Ocampa, stranding a combined Starfleet–Maquis crew some 75 years from home.

title: Enterprise-D destroyed at Veridian III
summary: An attack by the Duras sisters triggers a warp-core breach. The saucer section crash-lands on Veridian III and the crew survives, but the ship is lost.

title: Kirk dies on Veridian III
summary: Drawn out of the Nexus by Picard, James T. Kirk helps stop Dr. Tolian Soran from destroying the Veridian star and dies in the attempt, 78 years after he was presumed lost.

title: Tal Shiar–Obsidian Order fleet destroyed
summary: A joint Romulan–Cardassian fleet attacks the Founders' homeworld in the Omarion Nebula, only to fall into a Jem'Hadar trap. The Obsidian Order is destroyed and the Tal Shiar badly crippled.

title: Klingons invade Cardassia, quit Khitomer
summary: Suspecting Dominion influence in a Cardassian civilian uprising, Gowron invades the Cardassian Union. When the Federation condemns the attack, the Klingons withdraw from the Khitomer Accords.

title: USS Enterprise-E launched
summary: The Sovereign-class Enterprise-E launches from the San Francisco Fleet Yards under Captain Picard, about a year after the loss of the Enterprise-D.

title: Antwerp bombing; coup attempt on Earth
summary: A Changeling bombs a Federation–Romulan conference in Antwerp. Admiral Leyton exploits the fear to stage a coup against President Jaresh-Inyo, which Sisko exposes.

title: Federation–Klingon War of 2372–73
summary: With the alliance broken, the Federation and the Klingon Empire fight a brief but bitter war, provoked by a Changeling impersonating General Martok.

title: DTI investigates the Defiant's time jump
summary: Agents Dulmur and Lucsly of the Department of Temporal Investigations — an agency that did not yet exist in the 2260s — debrief Sisko after the Defiant is thrown back to Space Station K-7 in 2268. Kirk's file lists seventeen temporal violations.

title: Bajor's Federation entry deferred
summary: Acting on a vision as Emissary, Sisko persuades Bajor not to join the Federation on the eve of its admission. Months later Bajor signs a non-aggression pact with the Dominion, which spares it from the coming war.

title: Cardassia joins the Dominion
summary: Gul Dukat brings the Cardassian Union into the Dominion and Jem'Hadar fleets pour through the wormhole. Facing the threat, the Klingons rejoin the Khitomer Accords.

title: Battle of Sector 001
summary: A second Borg cube reaches Earth and is destroyed with the Enterprise-E's help. A sphere escapes to 2063 to stop Zefram Cochrane's warp flight, and Picard's crew follows to protect first contact.

title: Dominion War begins
summary: Starfleet mines the wormhole's mouth to stop Dominion reinforcements. The Dominion and Cardassians seize Deep Space 9, and full-scale war breaks out with the Federation–Klingon alliance.

title: First contact with Species 8472
summary: Voyager finds the Borg losing a war against Species 8472 from fluidic space. Janeway forges a temporary alliance with the Collective to build a weapon that drives the invaders back.

title: Operation Return retakes Deep Space 9
summary: A Federation–Klingon fleet breaks the Dominion line, and the Prophets erase a Dominion reinforcement fleet inside the wormhole. The allies retake the station.

title: Krenim timeship's Year of Hell
summary: Annorax's Krenim weapon ship rewrites Delta Quadrant history in search of a perfect restoration of his people, battering Voyager for a year. When it is destroyed, the timeline resets and the year never happens.

title: Voyager contacts Starfleet
summary: Sent through an alien relay network, Voyager's EMH reaches the USS Prometheus. Starfleet learns the ship survived, and letters from home follow.

title: Section 31 exposed
summary: Julian Bashir is tested by Section 31, a covert agency claiming authority from the original Starfleet Charter. It later infects the Founders with a lethal disease.

title: Romulans join the Dominion War
summary: The assassination of Senator Vreenak, made to look like a Dominion act by Garak with Sisko's reluctant approval, brings the Romulan Star Empire into the war on the allied side.

title: Battle of Chin'toka; wormhole closes
summary: The allies win their first major foothold in Cardassian space, but a Pah-wraith kills Jadzia Dax and seals the Bajoran wormhole, cutting Bajor off from the Prophets for months.

title: Ba'ku relocation halted
summary: Picard defies a Federation–Son'a plan to harvest the rejuvenating metaphasic radiation of the Ba'ku planet by secretly relocating its people.

title: Breen attack Starfleet Headquarters
summary: The Breen Confederacy joins the Dominion and raids San Francisco, damaging Starfleet Headquarters. Their energy-dampening weapon then devastates an allied fleet at Chin'toka.

title: Damar leads a Cardassian rebellion
summary: Legate Damar turns against the Dominion and leads a Cardassian Liberation Front. When Cardassia rises, the Dominion begins exterminating its population.

title: Martok becomes Klingon Chancellor
summary: Worf kills Gowron in combat after the Chancellor's reckless strategy endangers the war effort and hands leadership of the Empire to General Martok.

title: Rom becomes Grand Nagus
summary: Zek retires and names Rom his successor, handing him a Ferengi Alliance newly reformed with rights for women and the first social programs.

title: Dominion War ends
summary: The allies besiege Cardassia Prime; Odo links with the Female Changeling and cures her of the disease, and the Dominion surrenders. Some 800 million Cardassians have died.

title: Sisko joins the Prophets
summary: Defeating Dukat and the Pah-wraiths in the Fire Caves, Benjamin Sisko passes into the wormhole to live among the Prophets.

title: Pathfinder opens regular contact with Voyager
summary: Reginald Barclay's Pathfinder Project uses a micro-wormhole to open a communication link with Voyager, later a regular monthly exchange.

title: Arbiter rules the Doctor an artist
summary: A Federation arbiter rules that Voyager's EMH may control his holonovel as its artist, though not yet that he is a person — a first step for holographic rights.

title: Voyager returns to Earth
summary: An Admiral Janeway from 2404 travels back to guide Voyager home through a Borg transwarp hub, crippling the network and infecting the Borg Queen with a neurolytic pathogen.

title: Shinzon's Reman coup on Romulus
summary: Shinzon, a Reman-raised clone of Picard, wipes out the Romulan Senate with thalaron radiation and seizes power, then plots to destroy all life on Earth before dying at the Bassen Rift.

title: Data dies aboard the Scimitar
summary: Data sacrifices himself to destroy Shinzon's thalaron weapon and save Picard; his memories live on in the prototype android B-4.

title: Riker takes command of USS Titan
summary: Newly promoted, Captain William Riker leaves the Enterprise-E to command the Luna-class Titan and leads a task force to the Romulan Neutral Zone as the Federation opens talks with the post-Shinzon government.

title: Starfleet begins the Romulan evacuation
summary: Warned that the Romulan star will go supernova, the Star Empire asks for help. Picard is promoted to admiral and leaves the Enterprise-E to lead a rescue armada meant to move 900 million Romulans.

title: Ferenginar begins joining the Federation
summary: Under Grand Nagus Rom, and with its trade routes battered by raids from the rogue ship Nova One, Ferenginar begins the formal process of joining the Federation, overseen by Captain Carol Freeman.

title: Voyager retired to the Fleet Museum
summary: The Cerritos prepares the famous USS Voyager for its final trip to Earth, where it is placed on display in the Starfleet Fleet Museum.
sources: I Have No Bones Yet I Must Flee (episode)

title: Quantum fissures erupt across the multiverse
summary: Rifts into parallel universes open across Federation space, triggered by a ship exploring the multiverse. The Cerritos, tasked with sealing them, ends up confronting the crisis at its source.

title: USS Protostar launched with proto-warp
summary: Starfleet's experimental Protostar, driven by a captured proto-star, departs San Francisco under Captain Chakotay; it is soon lost in the Delta Quadrant.

title: Living Construct attacks the fleet
summary: The Diviner's Living Construct, hidden aboard the Protostar, turns a gathering of Starfleet ships against each other. The Protostar is sacrificed to destroy it, and its young crew is admitted to Starfleet.

title: USS Voyager-A launched
summary: Vice Admiral Kathryn Janeway takes the new Voyager-A on its maiden voyage in search of the missing Chakotay; Chakotay later takes command.

title: Vau N'Akat time war averted
summary: Asencia, a Vau N'Akat agent from the future, tries to turn a temporal paradox into a weapon against the Federation. The Prodigy cadets return the Protostar to its proper place in time, and Voyager-A makes official first contact with the Vau N'Akat.

title: Synth attack on Mars
summary: On First Contact Day, synthetic workers — secretly subverted by the Zhat Vash — destroy the Utopia Planitia Fleet Yards and the Romulan rescue armada, setting Mars ablaze and killing over 92,000 people.

title: Federation bans synthetic life
summary: The Federation outlaws the research, development and creation of synthetic lifeforms. Starfleet scales back and abandons the Romulan evacuation.

title: Picard resigns from Starfleet
summary: Admiral Picard quits in protest when Starfleet abandons the Romulan rescue, retiring to his family vineyard in France for fourteen years.

title: Romulan sun goes supernova
summary: The Romulan star explodes, destroying Romulus and Remus before Spock can contain it with red matter. The Star Empire collapses, and the Neutral Zone it guarded ceases to exist.
conflict: Star Trek (2009) says the supernova threatened the whole galaxy; PIC 'Remembrance' identifies the Romulan sun itself as the star. The name 'Hobus' for the exploding star is non-canon; the canonical Hobus system still exists in 3196.

title: Spock and Nero fall into the past
summary: The red-matter singularity swallows Spock's Jellyfish and Nero's Narada and throws them back in time into a new reality: Nero emerges in 2233 and Spock in 2258. Neither returns.

title: Romulan Free State rises
summary: From the wreckage of the Star Empire, the Tal Shiar-backed Romulan Free State emerges as the leading successor power, running the derelict Borg cube it calls the Artifact.

title: USS Titan-A launched
summary: The Neo-Constitution-class Titan-A enters service under Captain Liam Shaw; six years later it will be renamed Enterprise.

title: Coppelius standoff; synth ban lifted
summary: A Romulan fleet sent by the Zhat Vash to exterminate the synths of Coppelius withdraws after Picard persuades the synths to abandon their summons of machine super-intelligences and Starfleet arrives. The Federation lifts the synth ban after fourteen years.

title: Picard's mind moved to a synthetic body
summary: Picard dies of his brain abnormality and his consciousness is transferred into a synthetic 'golem' body. Data's consciousness, preserved in a quantum simulation, is ended at his request.

title: Q's Confederation timeline undone
summary: Q shifts Picard and his companions into an alternate 2401 ruled by the xenophobic Confederation of Earth. They travel to Los Angeles in 2024 to repair the divergence and restore history.

title: A new Borg collective joins the Federation
summary: A cooperative Borg collective, born in 2024 of Agnes Jurati and an alternate Borg Queen, reappears through a transwarp conduit and is granted provisional Federation membership to seal a dangerous spatial anomaly.

title: USS Voyager-B readied for launch
summary: A third Voyager, NCC-74656-B, is scheduled for launch as a contemporary of the Enterprise-F.

title: Changeling infiltration of Starfleet exposed
summary: Picard's crew uncovers renegade Changelings who have infiltrated Starfleet with new, undetectable shapeshifting, working with Vadic and the Shrike as agents of a larger Borg plot.

title: Enterprise-D restored for one last flight
summary: Geordi La Forge has spent two decades restoring the salvaged Enterprise-D at the Fleet Museum. Untouched by the Borg link, it is the only ship able to fly against the Collective on Frontier Day.

title: Frontier Day: Borg seize the fleet
summary: On the 250th Frontier Day, a Borg signal hidden in Starfleet's unified Fleet Formation links the fleet's young officers to the Collective and turns the ships against Earth. The recommissioned Enterprise-D's crew destroys the Borg Queen's cube.

title: Enterprise-F retired after Frontier Day
summary: Admiral Elizabeth Shelby's Odyssey-class flagship, slated for early decommissioning, is turned against Earth on Frontier Day; Shelby is killed by her own assimilated crew.

title: Borg Collective destroyed
summary: With the Queen and her cube destroyed over Jupiter, the Borg Collective is believed to be finished and the assimilated officers are freed.

title: Titan-A rechristened Enterprise-G
summary: A year after Frontier Day, the Neo-Constitution-class Titan-A is renamed USS Enterprise NCC-1701-G in honor of the Enterprise-D crew, with Captain Seven of Nine in command.

title: Admiral Janeway leaves 2404 to rewrite history
summary: In a future where Voyager took 23 years to return, an aging Admiral Janeway obtains a Klingon chronal deflector and travels back to 2378 to bring her crew home sooner, erasing her own timeline.

title: Barzan II joins the Federation
summary: Some time in the 25th century the Barzans, once too poor to join, become Federation members.

title: Time pod stolen from a 26th-century historian
summary: A 26th-century historian's time pod is stolen by the 22nd-century inventor Berlinghoff Rasmussen, who uses it to pose as a historian aboard the Enterprise-D in 2368 before Picard's crew sends him back.

title: Battle of Procyon V
summary: In a future shown to Archer by Daniels, a Federation fleet that counts Klingons and Xindi among its citizens defeats the Sphere-Builders at Procyon V and drives them back into their own realm.
conflict: Seen only in a vision from Daniels; the Sphere-Builders' spheres were destroyed in 2154 ('Zero Hour'), so whether this battle still happens is uncertain.

title: USS Enterprise-J in service
summary: The Universe-class USS Enterprise NCC-1701-J, a ship far larger than any 22nd-century vessel, takes part in the Battle of Procyon V.

title: Last known contact with the Q
summary: The Federation's last known contact with the Q Continuum happens around 2590; by the 32nd century the Q are a distant memory.

title: Last crossing to the mirror universe
summary: The final known crossing between the prime and mirror universes takes place; afterward the two realities drift apart and travel between them is thought impossible.

title: Kal Dano creates the Tox Uthat
summary: The scientist Kal Dano builds the Tox Uthat, a quantum phase inhibitor able to stop a star's fusion, and hides it on 22nd-century Risa to keep it from thieves. Two Vorgon criminals from his era hunt it in 2366.

title: Voyager's EMH adopts an aging program
summary: The Doctor from USS Voyager, still active three centuries after his ship came home, adds an aging subroutine to his matrix; he will still be teaching at Starfleet Academy in the 3190s.

title: The Cabal's future patron
summary: The faceless figure who directs the Suliban Cabal's operations in the Temporal Cold War is said to come from the 28th century.

title: Temporal Accord governs time travel
summary: An interstellar Temporal Accord permits time travel only for research and forbids changing history; Federation anthropologists from 2769 observe the building of the Great Pyramid under its rules.

title: Temporal Integrity Commission polices history
summary: The 29th-century Federation's Temporal Integrity Commission sends timeships such as the Aeon and the USS Relativity under Captain Braxton to detect and repair temporal incursions anywhere in history.

title: Temporal explosion destroys Sol (erased)
summary: In a timeline later erased, a 20th-century industrialist flies a stolen timeship to the 29th century and triggers an explosion that destroys the Sol system, prompting Braxton's mission to destroy Voyager in 2373.

title: The Temporal Wars
summary: For most of the 30th century the Federation fights a series of Temporal Wars to uphold the Temporal Accords against factions using time travel to remake history.
conflict: ENT's Daniels, a time-traveling agent from the 31st century, operates after the Temporal Wars are said to have ended in the 30th century.

title: Galactic dilithium begins to run out
summary: Known dilithium supplies begin drying up, and the Federation starts experimenting with alternative warp drive designs.

title: 31st-century temporal agents
summary: In Daniels's era time travel is so commonplace that quantum discriminators sit in school desks, and agents like him cross history to enforce the Temporal Accord against rival Cold War factions.

title: Khi'eth crashes in the Verubin Nebula
summary: The Kelpien research ship Khi'eth crashes on a dilithium planet deep in the Verubin Nebula. A rescue ship vanishes, and the only long-term survivor is Su'Kal, born there to a dying crew.

title: Starfleet Academy closes
summary: Starfleet Academy shuts its doors; it will not reopen for more than a century.

title: The Burn
summary: In an instant most dilithium in the galaxy goes inert and every active warp core explodes, killing millions. With warp travel crippled, the Federation begins to fragment and Qo'noS is devastated.
conflict: Booker (in 3188) and Vance (in 3189) both place it about 120 years earlier, putting it a year apart.

title: Burn devastates Qo'noS; Klingons scatter
summary: The Burn sets off matter–antimatter reactors across the Klingon homeworld and other worlds, rendering much of the Empire uninhabitable. The surviving Klingons scatter and the Great Houses dwindle to eight.

title: Doctor's backup revived in a Kyrian museum
summary: Seven centuries after Voyager's visit, a Kyrian curator reactivates a backup copy of its EMH. The Doctor corrects a warped history that cast Voyager as villains and helps bring peace between the Kyrians and Vaskans.

title: Emerald Chain rises after the Burn
summary: An Orion–Andorian mercantile syndicate grows in the chaos after the Burn into a de facto state, controlling dilithium and trade across much of the former Federation's space.

title: Earth leaves the Federation
summary: After the Burn, United Earth isolates itself and leaves the Federation. Federation headquarters and Starfleet move off Earth, and Titan breaks away.

title: Ni'Var leaves the Federation
summary: Ni'Var — Vulcan renamed after its people reunified with the Romulans — quits the Federation amid suspicion that its SB-19 research caused the Burn. No Federation ship visits it again for a century.

title: Betazed walls itself off
summary: Abandoned by the post-Burn Federation and ravaged by Venari Ral raids, the Betazoids raise a psionic wall around their star system; some thirty other worlds later shelter behind it, cut off from the galaxy for a century.

title: Temporal Accords ban all time travel
summary: Because of the Temporal Wars, the Temporal Accords are extended to outlaw time travel completely and time-travel technology is destroyed; by 3189 even the Federation has no way to send anyone through time.

title: Sahil begins a lonely Federation vigil
summary: Aditya Sahil becomes the lone keeper of a damaged Federation relay station and holds his post for some forty years, keeping his family's Federation flag — which, as a civilian, he may not raise — until Burnham commissions him in 3188.

title: Admiral Senna Tal calls believers to Earth
summary: On an obsolete Starfleet channel, Admiral Senna Tal broadcasts a call for anyone who still believes in the Federation to join him on Earth; the message later guides Burnham.

title: Burnham arrives in the 32nd century
summary: Michael Burnham emerges from the wormhole on Hima, sends the Red Angel suit back to fire the final signal, and spends a year as a courier with Cleveland Booker while waiting for Discovery.

title: Discovery reaches the 32nd century
summary: Discovery arrives a year after Burnham and finds a Federation shrunk from 350 member worlds to 38, run from a hidden headquarters. Admiral Vance welcomes it back into Starfleet with the registry NCC-1031-A.

title: Guardian of Forever found in hiding
summary: The Guardian of Forever, which fled the Temporal Wars, is found on Dannus V in the guise of 'Carl'. It sends the ailing Georgiou back to her own time.

title: Cause of the Burn discovered
summary: Discovery traces the Burn to Su'Kal, whose anguished cry resonated through the galaxy's dilithium; the nebula's dilithium world gives the Federation a way to rebuild warp travel.

title: Emerald Chain defeated at Federation HQ
summary: Osyraa's attempt to seize Discovery and Federation Headquarters fails. She is killed, and the Emerald Chain's grip on the region collapses.

title: Trill rejoins the Federation
summary: Trill becomes one of the first worlds to rejoin the Federation after the Burn's cause is solved.

title: Federation grows to 58 worlds
summary: With dilithium flowing again, 21 more worlds rejoin, Laira Rillak is elected President, and Starfleet Academy reopens after more than a century.

title: Dark Matter Anomaly destroys Kwejian
summary: A gravitational anomaly five light-years across rips through Kwejian and threatens worlds across the galaxy; it is later found to be an artificial mining device.

title: Ni'Var rejoins the Federation
summary: After a century apart, Ni'Var votes to rejoin the Federation under President T'Rina.

title: Discovery's AI Zora recognized as sentient
summary: The ship's computer, merged since 3189 with the ancient Sphere's archive, is judged a new sentient lifeform and enlisted as a Starfleet specialist.

title: First contact with Species 10-C
summary: Beyond the galactic barrier, a delegation of galactic powers led by Discovery reaches the extragalactic Species 10-C, whose mining had created the anomaly, and persuades them to stop.

title: United Earth rejoins the Federation
summary: Earth returns to the Federation it founded, a century after leaving it.

title: Red Directive hunt for Progenitor technology
summary: Under a classified Red Directive, Discovery follows clues hidden by 24th-century scientists toward the Progenitors' life-creating technology, racing the couriers Moll and L'ak and later the Breen.

title: Krenim chronophage traps Discovery in time
summary: A Krenim chronophage planted aboard sends Discovery skipping through its own past and future, including a 3218 in which the Breen have destroyed Federation Headquarters; the crew breaks free.

title: Breen Imperium torn by succession war
summary: The Breen Imperium, successor to the old Breen Confederacy, splits into warring factions over its leadership; rival Primarchs hunt the Progenitor technology, alarming Federation border worlds.

title: Progenitor technology left unclaimed
summary: Burnham reaches the Progenitors' interface inside a portal between binary black holes, refuses to use the power to create life, and the technology withdraws to await another finder. The Red Directive is closed and classified.

title: Kovich revealed as Agent Daniels
summary: The Federation's enigmatic intelligence chief Kovich tells Burnham his real name: Agent Daniels, the temporal agent who once served aboard Archer's Enterprise.

title: Starfleet Academy reopens in San Francisco
summary: The Academy welcomes its first San Francisco class in over a century under Chancellor Nahla Ake, with the USS Athena as training ship and Voyager's long-lived EMH on the faculty.
conflict: On-screen clues disagree: a personnel file and yearbook imply 3195–96, while the stardates convert to 3191–92, and DIS 'Kobayashi Maru' already shows the Academy reopened in 3190.

title: Betazed rejoins as the new Federation capital
summary: Betazed agrees to lower its psionic wall and rejoin the Federation on condition that it becomes the new Federation capital; the new seat of government is dedicated there in 3196.

title: Klingons settle New Qo'noS
summary: The Klingons, scattered since the Burn devastated Qo'noS, claim Faan Alpha as their new homeworld in a staged, bloodless 'conquest' arranged with the Federation, renaming it New Qo'noS.

title: Venari Ral ring the Federation with mines
summary: Nus Braka's Venari Ral seed Omega-47 mines — built around a synthetic Omega molecule stolen from Starbase J19-Alpha — around the core of Federation space.

title: Braka's show trial fails; Braka captured
summary: Nus Braka stages a broadcast 'Trial of the Federation' on the captured Sato Atrium while his Omega-47 mines hold worlds hostage. The USS Athena finds the atrium and seizes his mine-control frequency; Braka is arrested and discredited.

title: Discovery's final Red Directive mission
summary: Decades later, Admiral Burnham takes Discovery, restored to its original configuration, on one last mission: leaving the ship and its AI Zora in deep space to await someone called Craft.

title: Zora rescues Craft after a millennium
summary: After waiting about a thousand years, Discovery's AI Zora takes in Craft, a soldier adrift from a war between Alcor IV and the V'draysh, and sends him home in the ship's last shuttle.
